## `client.queries`

The `queries` resource of the platform API.

### `client.queries.list`

Signature: `client.queries.list(environment: str, *, include_ended: bool = False, status: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, submitter: str | None = None, limit: int = 100, cursor: str | None = None) -> list[QueryListEntry]`

List the queries of an environment: running, then queued, then (optionally) ended.

With `SUBMIT_QUERY` you see the queries you submitted (a task token: its own); with `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT` on the environment, everyone's. A row never holds the SQL text, an error message or a result, not even your own: read those through the query's status. Running queries come first, longest running first, then queued ones in the order they will be taken, with the reason each waits in `waiting_for`; with `include_ended`, then the queries that ended in the last 24 hours, newest first. `limit` cuts that order. `status` and `submitter` only narrow what you may see; `list_page` also returns the cursor of the next page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment. |
| `include_ended` | `bool` | `False` | Also list the queries that ended in the last 24 hours. |
| `status` | `str | Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Only queries in this status or one of these (``queued``, ``running``, ``succeeded``, ``failed``, ``cancelled``). An ended status lists the ended queries of the last 24 hours, with or without `include_ended`. |
| `submitter` | `str | None` | `None` | Only the queries submitted by the principal with this name. |
| `limit` | `int` | `100` | Most entries returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same filters with every page. |

Returns: `list of QueryListEntry`. The entries, in the order above.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not submit queries in this environment. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `limit` is outside 1 to 200, a status is unknown, or `cursor` is not one the server issued for the queries list. |

### `client.queries.list_page`

Signature: `client.queries.list_page(environment: str, *, include_ended: bool = False, status: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, submitter: str | None = None, limit: int = 100, cursor: str | None = None) -> QueryListPage`

List one page of the queries of an environment, with the cursor of the next page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment. |
| `include_ended` | `bool` | `False` | Also list the queries that ended in the last 24 hours. |
| `status` | `str | Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Only queries in this status or one of these (``queued``, ``running``, ``succeeded``, ``failed``, ``cancelled``). |
| `submitter` | `str | None` | `None` | Only the queries submitted by the principal with this name. |
| `limit` | `int` | `100` | Most entries returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same filters with every page. |

Returns: `QueryListPage`. The entries in the order of `list`, and the cursor for the next page (`None` on the last).

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not submit queries in this environment. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `limit` is outside 1 to 200, a status is unknown, or `cursor` is not one the server issued for the queries list. |

### `client.queries.submit`

Signature: `client.queries.submit(sql: str, environment: str, *, into: str | None = None, mode: str | None = None, incremental_key: str | None = None, evolve_schema: bool = False, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> QueryRun`

Submit a query for execution.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sql` | `str` | required | The SQL text to run. |
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment to run the query against. |
| `into` | `str | None` | `None` | Write the result into this table or view. |
| `mode` | `str | None` | `None` | `create`, `replace`, `append` or `view`. |
| `incremental_key` | `str | None` | `None` | With `mode="append"`, append only rows whose key is past the target's maximum. |
| `evolve_schema` | `bool` | `False` | Let the target adopt the result's schema. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |

Returns: `QueryRun`. A handle for polling status and fetching results.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the write options don't go together. |

### `client.queries.get`

Signature: `client.queries.get(query_id: str, environment: str) -> QueryRun`

Build a handle for an already-submitted query.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_id` | `str` | required | The query's id. |
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment the query runs against. |

Returns: `QueryRun`. A handle for polling status and fetching results. No request is sent until the handle is used.

### `client.queries.cancel`

Signature: `client.queries.cancel(query_id: str, environment: str) -> QueryStatus`

Cancel a query by id; the same call as `get(query_id, environment).cancel()`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_id` | `str` | required | The query's id. |
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment the query runs against. |

Returns: `QueryStatus`. The query's status after the request: `CANCELLED`, still `RUNNING` (it ends within the server's grace period), or the final status of a query that had already ended.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the query does not exist, or you neither submitted it nor hold `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT` on its environment. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the query is the write of a pipeline task (cancel the run) or a maintenance run that has started. |
